name: Wesley Harcourt, Med-Surg: UTI and autonomic dysreflexia in chronic T4 spinal cord injury (in class) (draft)

caseMeta.title: In-class SCI (draft): febrile UTI and autonomic dysreflexia in a man with a chronic complete T4 spinal cord injury (24 hours, checkpoints every 4 hours)
learningObjectives: Read vital signs against the baseline of a person with a high spinal cord injury (low resting BP, poor temperature control) and recognize how infection presents without sensation below the injury.

Recognize autonomic dysreflexia and carry out the nursing actions in order: sit up and lower the legs, loosen tight items, check BP every 2-5 minutes, find and remove the cause (bladder first, then bowel, then skin), notify the provider, give an antihypertensive only if SBP stays 150 or more, and monitor for 2 hours.
Question order-set call parameters that do not fit the patient, and remove an indwelling catheter by its nurse-driven criteria.
Prevent and manage the complications of SCI: pressure injury, orthostatic hypotension, neurogenic bowel and bladder, weak cough, VTE; follow a culture-guided antibiotic change and teach prevention.

notes.title: ED Triage Nursing Note
notes.author: G. Sotelo, RN
notes.summary: 34-year-old man with chronic T4 complete spinal cord injury: fever, chills, cloudy foul urine, more spasms and leaking between caths. T 101.8 F, HR 98, BP 92/56 ("my normal is 95 over 60").
notes.body:
**Arrival 2130** with his sister, Claire Harcourt (31, emergency contact), who drove him in. Arrived in his own manual wheelchair.

**Triage 2140**
T 101.8 F (38.8 C), HR 98, BP 92/56, RR 18, SpO2 96% on room air. Pain 2/10 (shoulders, chronic). Alert, oriented x4. Weight 72.0 kg (bed scale). Shows his AD wallet card: "My normal BP is 95 over 60."

**History (patient)**
- T4 complete spinal cord injury from a car crash 02/2025; self-catheterizes every 4-6 hours (14 Fr); bowel program every evening at 2000.
- Saturday: urine cloudier with a strong smell, two leaks between caths, more leg spasms.
- Sunday: chills by noon, "just feeling off," tired. Sat in his wheelchair most of the day in damp clothes and skipped pressure reliefs. At 1600 a stuffy nose and headache when his bladder got full; gone after he cathed. Home temperature 101.6 F at 2000.
- No burning or flank pain he can feel (no sensation below T4).
- 2 UTIs in the past year, both treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (last 10/2026).
- Allergy: penicillin (rash as a child).

**Plan**
Provider notified at 2145. Placed on a stretcher with a pillow under the calves. Asked staff to "please check my skin, I sat all day."

notes.title: ED Provider Note - Febrile UTI in Spinal Cord Injury
notes.author: P. Tolliver, MD
notes.summary: Febrile complicated UTI in chronic T4 SCI with neurogenic bladder. UA nitrite positive, LE 3+; WBC 14.6; lactate 1.6; procalcitonin 0.42. Cultures sent; ceftriaxone 1 g; 1 L NS. New stage 2 sacral pressure injury. Admit.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Fever and cloudy, foul-smelling urine.

**HPI**
34-year-old man with a chronic complete T4 spinal cord injury (AIS A, 02/2025) and a reflex neurogenic bladder managed with intermittent catheterization. Two days of cloudy, foul urine, leaking between caths and more spasms; chills and fever since Sunday noon (home 101.6 F). A brief episode of stuffy nose and headache at 1600 with a full bladder, resolved after cathing. He cannot feel burning or flank pain. Two UTIs in the past year treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

**Exam**
T 101.8 F, HR 98, BP 92/56 (baseline about 95/60 on his AD card), RR 18, SpO2 96% RA. Alert, oriented. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Sensory level T4; no movement of the legs. Sacrum: new stage 2 pressure injury 2.0 x 1.5 cm.

**Results**
- UA (new catheter): cloudy, nitrite positive, leukocyte esterase 3+, WBC over 50/hpf with clumps, many bacteria, squamous cells 0-2.
- WBC 14.6 (neutrophils 84%, bands 4%). Hgb 13.4. Platelets 262.
- Na 136, K 4.2, Cl 102, CO2 23, BUN 22, creatinine 0.7. Anion gap 136 - 102 - 23 = 11. BUN/creatinine 31 (mild volume loss).
- Lactate 1.6. Procalcitonin 0.42. CRP 98. ESR 48.

**Assessment**
Febrile complicated UTI (likely upper tract) in a man with a neurogenic bladder. Not septic shock: lactate normal; the low BP is his baseline (an SBP of 92 scores a qSOFA point but is his normal). New stage 2 sacral pressure injury.

**Plan**
Blood cultures x2 and urine culture sent before antibiotics. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV (childhood penicillin rash only). 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L, then 100 mL/h. Acetaminophen. Indwelling catheter for now. Discussed with Dr. Haverty: admit to 4 West Medical-Surgical; no bed until morning.

AD history: AD protocol and nitroglycerin PRN ordered; sildenafil held. Enoxaparin for SCI clot risk. Continue baclofen.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Fever and cloudy urine.

**HPI**
See the ED note. Febrile UTI after 2 days of cloudy foul urine, leaking and more spasms in a man with a chronic T4 complete injury who self-catheterizes.

**Past history**
- **T4 fracture-dislocation, complete (AIS A), neurological level T4** from a motor vehicle crash 02/14/2025; posterior fusion T2-T6 02/15/2025; spinal shock resolved over about 6 weeks; 8 weeks inpatient rehab.
- Neurogenic (reflex) bladder: intermittent catheterization every 4-6 h, 14 Fr hydrophilic catheter, volumes 350-450 mL. 2 UTIs in the last year (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, last 10/2026).
- Neurogenic bowel: program every evening at 2000 (senna at noon, bisacodyl suppository with lidocaine jelly, digital stimulation).
- **Autonomic dysreflexia: 3 episodes at home** (09/2025 full bladder, SBP about 160; 01/2026 ingrown toenail; 06/2026 tight shoes and a folded leg strap). Carries an AD card (baseline 95/60). First sign for him: "stuffy nose, then the headache."
- Orthostatic hypotension: uses an abdominal binder and thigh-high compression stockings.
- Stage 2 pressure injury right ischium during rehab (2025), healed.
- Mild depression in the first year after injury; counseling finished 2026.

**Medications** Baclofen 10 mg three times a day; oxybutynin 5 mg three times a day; senna 17.2 mg at noon; docusate 100 mg twice a day; bisacodyl 10 mg suppository at 2000; lidocaine 2% jelly; vitamin D3 2,000 units daily; sildenafil 50 mg PRN (last about 10 days ago); acetaminophen PRN.

**Allergy** Penicillin (rash as a child; no hives or swelling).

**Social** Lives alone in an accessible apartment; works from home (software quality testing). Personal care attendant 3 mornings a week. Sister Claire nearby (emergency contact). Drives with hand controls. Never smoked; 2-4 beers a week.

**Exam** T 100.4 F, HR 84, BP 96/58, RR 16, SpO2 97% RA (0100). Alert, oriented x4. Arms 5/5; legs 0/5, increased tone. Light touch and pinprick normal through T4, absent T5 and below; no anal sensation or voluntary contraction. Lungs clear, weak cough. Abdomen soft. Sacrum: stage 2, 2.0 x 1.5 x 0.1 cm.

**Data** WBC 14.6; UA nitrite positive, LE 3+; lactate 1.6; procalcitonin 0.42; CRP 98; creatinine 0.7 (low muscle mass: creatinine-based eGFR overestimates his kidney function).

**Assessment and plan**
1. **Complicated UTI, febrile**: ceftriaxone 1 g IV every 24 h; follow the urine and blood cultures (his usual home antibiotic may not work: 2 courses this year). Acetaminophen PRN. 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL/h.
2. **Neurogenic bladder**: indwelling catheter for now; RN may remove it when afebrile 8 h, IV fluids off and hourly output not needed, then intermittent catheterization every 4 h. Oxybutynin.
3. **Autonomic dysreflexia risk**: nurse-driven AD protocol; nitroglycerin 2% ointment PRN for SBP 150 or more after the cause search; hold sildenafil. **His baseline SBP is 90-100; BP 92-98 tonight is his normal.**
4. **Stage 2 sacral pressure injury (present on admission)**: low-air-loss mattress, turn every 2 h, foam dressing, wound nurse, dietitian.
5. **VTE prophylaxis**: enoxaparin 40 mg SubQ daily (SCI with immobility plus acute infection).
6. **Spasticity**: continue baclofen; do not stop suddenly.
7. **Neurogenic bowel**: home program at 2000 with lidocaine jelly.
8. Orthostatic hypotension: binder and stockings before sitting up. Incentive spirometer, assisted cough.
9. AM labs; PT, OT, physiatry, pharmacy, case management. Full Code.

**S** Wesley (Wes) Harcourt, 34, coming to 4W-14: complicated UTI (febrile) with a neurogenic bladder, chronic T4 complete spinal cord injury; new stage 2 sacral pressure injury found in the ED. Full Code. Penicillin allergy (childhood rash).

**B** Injury 02/2025, wheelchair user, lives alone, self-caths every 4-6 h, bowel program at 2000 nightly (missed Sunday). 3 episodes of autonomic dysreflexia at home; carries an AD card.

**A** Last set 0400: T 99.8, HR 74, BP 94/58, RR 16, SpO2 97%. His BP runs in the 90s; that is normal for him. Left forearm 20 g with 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL/h. 16 Fr indwelling catheter, cloudy amber urine; bag emptied 0645. Ceftriaxone 1 g given 2300. Acetaminophen 0430. Sacrum: foam dressing. Lay on an ED stretcher about 9 hours.

**R** Low-air-loss mattress on 4 West. Turn every 2 h. Home meds per admission orders (baclofen: do not miss). Check his skin and the catheter tubing with every turn. Med rec by pharmacy this morning.

notes.title: Pharmacy Note - Medication Reconciliation
notes.author: F. Ashby, PharmD
notes.summary: Home meds reconciled. Penicillin childhood rash: ceftriaxone OK (low cross-reactivity). Baclofen: do not stop. Sildenafil last about 10 days ago: no nitrate conflict now; keep held. Enoxaparin 40 mg daily fits weight and kidney function (eGFR overestimates in SCI).
notes.body:
**Sources** Patient (very reliable; carries a med list), sister, outpatient pharmacy fill history.

**Home medications** baclofen 10 mg TID; oxybutynin 5 mg TID; sennosides 17.2 mg daily at noon; docusate 100 mg BID; bisacodyl 10 mg suppository daily at 2000; lidocaine 2% jelly PRN; cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily; sildenafil 50 mg PRN (last dose 02/26, per patient); acetaminophen 650 mg PRN. All ordered except sildenafil (held).

**Checks**
- **Allergy**: penicillin, rash as a child, no hives or swelling. Cross-reactivity with a third-generation cephalosporin is very low; ceftriaxone appropriate.
- **Baclofen**: do not hold or stop suddenly (withdrawal: seizures, high fever, rebound spasticity). If he cannot swallow, call for another route.
- **Sildenafil and nitrates**: nitroglycerin PRN is ordered for AD. No sildenafil in the last 24 hours (last about 10 days ago), so nitroglycerin may be used if needed. Keep sildenafil held while in the hospital.
- **Enoxaparin 40 mg SubQ daily**: weight 72.0 kg; creatinine 0.6, eGFR 130. Creatinine is low from low muscle mass after SCI, so the eGFR overestimates kidney function; still well above the dose-change cutoff (CrCl under 30).
- **Oxybutynin**: anticholinergic; can add to constipation and poor sweating. Continue (home bladder regimen).
- Ceftriaxone next dose Mon 2300.

notes.title: Charge Nurse Event Note - Autonomic Dysreflexia
notes.author: K. Thibodeaux, RN
notes.summary: Autonomic dysreflexia 0912-0950 from kinked catheter tubing under the left thigh. BP peak 204/112, HR 46. Sat up, legs down, binder and stockings loosened, kink straightened: 600 mL drained. No antihypertensive needed. Provider notified 0918. BP every 15 min to 1150.
notes.body:
**Called to 4W-14 at 0916** by the day RN.

**Timeline**
- 0905: goose bumps on his arms and a stuffy nose (he thought it was the room).
- 0912: sudden pounding headache 8/10 at the back of the head, blurred vision; he called.
- 0915: BP 164/94, HR 62. Face, neck and upper chest flushed and sweaty; skin below the nipple line pale and cool with goose bumps. Anxious. He said: "This is dysreflexia. Check my bladder." Drainage bag had 0 mL since it was emptied at 0730.
- 0916: head of bed raised to 90 degrees and legs lowered (chair position). Charge RN at the bedside; second RN called Dr. Kincaid at 0918.
- 0917: BP 182/102, HR 54. Abdominal binder, both thigh-high compression stockings and the gown ties loosened.
- 0919: BP 196/108, HR 48. Catheter traced from the meatus to the bag.
- 0920: BP 204/112, HR 46. **Tubing kinked under the left thigh** (he was boosted up in bed for his breakfast tray at 0730). Kink straightened: cloudy amber urine flowed fast.
- 0921: Dr. Kincaid by phone: continue the protocol; 12-lead ECG; nitroglycerin ointment only if SBP stays 150 or more after the bladder is empty; call back in 15 minutes.
- 0923: BP 172/98, HR 50. 12-lead ECG done. About 400 mL drained.
- 0925: BP 156/90, HR 56. Headache 6/10. Drainage finished 0926: **600 mL** total. Not clamped.
- 0927: BP 144/86, HR 58: SBP under 150 and falling with the cause removed, so **nitroglycerin not given**. Sildenafil: last dose about 10 days ago.
- 0930: BP 132/80, HR 62. Headache 4/10; flushing fading. Bladder scan 30 mL. Catheter secured to the left thigh with a securement device; bag below the bladder, off the floor; tubing straight.
- 0935 120/74 HR 64; 0940 114/70 HR 66; 0945 110/68 HR 66 (headache 2/10; neuro check normal: arms strong, speech clear, pupils equal).
- 0950: BP 108/66, HR 66. Symptoms gone. **Resolved.**

**Plan**
BP and HR every 15 minutes for 2 hours (to 1150), then per order. Abdominal binder and stockings stay off for now; put them back on before he sits up. Check the tubing with every turn and every 2 hours. Dr. Kincaid coming to the bedside.

**Patient**
Tired and embarrassed: "I should have felt it coming sooner." Reassured; he recognized it and told us exactly what to check.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Event Note - Autonomic Dysreflexia
notes.author: M. Kincaid, MD
notes.summary: AD 0912-0950 from a kinked catheter, resolved without medicine (peak 204/112, HR 46). ECG sinus bradycardia 50, no ischemia. Call parameters corrected (SBP 130 or more or any AD symptom). Stop NS at 1100. Blood cultures no growth at 12 hours.
notes.body:
**Event**
Seen at the bedside at 1005. Autonomic dysreflexia from 0912 to 0950: kinked catheter tubing under the left thigh after he was boosted up at 0730. BP peaked at 204/112 with HR 46 at 0920. Nursing sat him up, lowered his legs, loosened the binder and stockings, found and straightened the kink: 600 mL drained. SBP was under 150 by 0927 with the cause removed: nitroglycerin correctly not given. Now 104/62, HR 68, headache 1/10, neuro exam normal.

**ECG 0923** Sinus bradycardia 50, PR 180 ms, QRS 80 ms, no ST or T-wave changes. The slow rate is the reflex (vagal) response to the high BP. No ischemia.

**Results** Blood cultures: no growth at 12 hours (1000). Morning labs: WBC 13.1, creatinine 0.6, Mg 1.9, CRP 112, albumin 3.2.

**Assessment** AD from bladder distension, resolved with removal of the cause. The 0115 order-set call parameters (SBP greater than 160 or less than 90) do not fit him: his baseline SBP is 90-100, so AD starts at 120-140, and an SBP under 90 fires at his normal. Corrected.

**Plan**
- New call parameters: SBP 130 or more, OR any AD symptom at any BP; SBP under 80 or a symptomatic drop on sitting up; HR under 50 or over 110; temperature over 100.4 F; SpO2 under 92%.
- BP every 15 minutes until 1150, then every 4 hours.
- Catheter secured to the thigh; tubing checks every 2 hours and with every turn.
- Stop 0.9% sodium chloride at 1100 and saline-lock (drinking well).
- CBC and CRP at 1700. Continue ceftriaxone. Enoxaparin today (delayed by the event).
- Binder and stockings back on before he sits up for therapy.

notes.title: Wound/Ostomy Nursing Consult - Sacrum
notes.author: L. Dunleavy, RN, CWOCN
notes.summary: Stage 2 sacral pressure injury (present on admission), 2.0 x 1.5 x 0.1 cm, clean. No culture (no signs of infection). Silicone foam every 3 days; low-air-loss mattress, 30-degree turns, own cushion, limit sitting to 1 h. Prealbumin 14 is low but must be read with CRP 112.
notes.body:
**Wound** Sacrum, stage 2 pressure injury, present on admission (found in the ED 03/07 2210). 2.0 x 1.5 x 0.1 cm. Pink, moist wound bed; partial thickness; no slough, eschar or tunneling. Scant serous drainage. No odor. Periwound skin intact, no redness spreading, no warmth. Right ischium and both heels intact (old right ischial scar intact).

**Cause** About 12 hours sitting in his wheelchair in damp clothes on Sunday without pressure reliefs while feverish, then about 9 hours on an ED stretcher without an overlay.

**Culture?** No. A clean stage 2 wound with no signs of infection should not be swabbed: a swab grows skin bacteria and leads to unneeded antibiotics.

**Nutrition labs** Prealbumin 14 and albumin 3.2 are low, but both fall with inflammation (CRP 112 this morning), so they are not a pure nutrition marker. Dietitian consulted.

**Plan**
- Cleanse with 0.9% sodium chloride; silicone foam border dressing; change every 3 days (next Wed 03/10) and as needed if soiled or lifting.
- Low-air-loss mattress. Turn every 2 h, 30-degree side-lying, never flat on the sacrum; heels floated.
- In the chair: his own air-cell cushion only; pressure relief every 15 minutes; limit sitting to 1 hour at a time until the sacrum is healing.
- Check the skin under the binder, stockings and catheter securement with each turn.
- Braden 13 (moderate risk).

notes.title: Nutrition Note - Pressure Injury
notes.author: E. Wexford, RD
notes.summary: Protein goal 90-108 g/day (1.25-1.5 g/kg), fluids about 2.2 L. High-protein supplement twice a day; multivitamin. Vitamin D level pending.
notes.body:
**Data** Weight 72.0 kg (usual 74 kg, 11/2026). Height 180 cm. BMI 72.0 / 3.24 = 22.2. Low muscle mass below T4. Albumin 3.2, prealbumin 14 (both lowered by inflammation; CRP 112). 25-hydroxy vitamin D: level pending.

**Intake** Ate about 50% of meals Saturday and Sunday; breakfast today about 75%.

**Needs**
- Protein for a pressure injury: 1.25-1.5 g/kg = 1.25 x 72 = 90 to 1.5 x 72 = 108 g/day.
- Fluid: 30 mL/kg = 30 x 72 = 2,160 mL/day (about 2.2 L), spread over the day, less after 2000 (fewer night caths).

**Plan** High-protein diet; high-protein oral supplement 1 bottle twice a day (1000 and 1600); multivitamin with minerals daily. Protein at every meal. Continue vitamin D3 2,000 units daily (adjust when the level is back). Fiber and fluids for the bowel program.

notes.title: Physical Therapy Evaluation
notes.author: B. Marchand, PT, DPT
notes.summary: Orthostatic drop 98/60 to 76/46 at 3 min sitting without the binder; 90/56 and tolerated with the binder, stockings and a slow raise. Independent slide-board transfers.
notes.body:
**Orthostatic vital signs**
- 1345 supine: 98/60, HR 70, no symptoms.
- 1346 sitting edge of bed 1 minute (binder NOT back on since the morning episode): 82/50, HR 84, lightheaded.
- 1348 sitting 3 minutes: **76/46**, HR 88, "my vision is going dim," yawning. Reclined with legs up: 96/58 at 1351, resolved.
- Drop: 98 - 76 = **22** systolic and 60 - 46 = **14** diastolic = orthostatic hypotension.
- 1400 after abdominal binder snug, thigh-high stockings on, head of bed raised over 10 minutes: sitting 3 minutes **90/56**, HR 80, no symptoms (98 - 90 = 8: not orthostatic).

**Function** Full arm strength. Independent slide-board transfer bed to tilt-in-space chair with set-up; sat 20 minutes. Independent pressure reliefs (forward lean).

**Plan** Binder and stockings on before every sit. Raise the head of the bed in stages. Tilt-in-space chair until his own wheelchair and cushion arrive. Daily therapy.

notes.title: Occupational Therapy Evaluation
notes.author: C. Pruneda, OTR/L
notes.summary: Independent self-catheterization and bowel care with set-up; pressure reliefs every 15 min; needs his own cushion; uses a long-handled mirror.
notes.body:
**ADLs** Independent with self-catheterization (14 Fr hydrophilic) and bowel care with set-up; independent upper-body dressing; needs help with lower-body dressing and stockings (attendant at home).

**Skin** Checks his skin morning and evening with a long-handled mirror. Right ischium was red after 45 minutes in a hospital wheelchair without his cushion; faded in 20 minutes. Needs his own air-cell cushion (sister bringing it). Pressure reliefs every 15-30 minutes at home; every 15 minutes here while the sacrum heals.

**Plan** Set-up for self-caths once the indwelling catheter is out. Mirror at the bedside. Practice putting on the binder.

notes.title: Physiatry Consult - Spinal Cord Injury
notes.author: J. Okerlund, DO
notes.summary: Chronic T4 AIS A with AD this morning from a catheter kink. Remove the indwelling catheter tonight and resume intermittent catheterization every 4 h (under 500 mL). Lidocaine before bowel care. Vitamin D 22: continue 2,000 units, recheck in 3 months. AD card reviewed. SCI clinic in 2 weeks.
notes.body:
**Reason** Chronic SCI with UTI and autonomic dysreflexia.

**Findings** T4 AIS A (complete), neurological level T4, unchanged from his clinic exam. AD this morning from a kinked catheter, handled well (sit up, loosen, bladder first). Orthostatic hypotension at therapy without the binder. Stage 2 sacrum.

**Recommendations**
1. **Bladder**: remove the indwelling catheter tonight if he stays afebrile (the order's criteria); resume intermittent catheterization every 4 hours, volumes under 500 mL. Bladder scan if over 500 mL or with any AD sign. An indwelling catheter adds infection risk and, as today showed, can kink.
2. **Bowel**: home program tonight at 2000; lidocaine 2% jelly before the suppository and digital stimulation; stop and follow the AD protocol if symptoms. He has had no BM for 2 days: bowel is the second most common AD trigger.
3. **AD**: card reviewed with him (baseline 95/60). Prevention: catheter on time, tubing checks, loose clothing, skin checks, nail care.
4. **Orthostatic hypotension**: binder and stockings before sitting; no medicine needed now.
5. **Vitamin D 22** (insufficient): continue 2,000 units daily; recheck in 3 months.
6. **Spasticity**: baclofen unchanged; increased spasms should settle as the infection clears.
7. Follow-up: SCI clinic (Dr. H. Bergeron) in 2 weeks.

notes.title: Case Management Note
notes.author: R. Varnado, RN CM
notes.summary: Lives alone; personal care attendant 3 mornings/week; sister nearby. Home health nursing for wound checks twice weekly. Plan home Tuesday if afebrile on an oral antibiotic.
notes.body:
**Home** Accessible ground-floor apartment, alone. Works full time from home. Personal care attendant (Andre Lusk) 3 mornings a week. Sister Claire 15 minutes away; she brought his air-cell cushion and supplies at 1600.

**Equipment** Own manual wheelchair, air-cell cushion, padded commode chair, intermittent catheters, binder, stockings. Asks about a pressure-redistribution mattress overlay for home: request sent to the outpatient SCI clinic.

**Plan** Home health nursing twice a week for the sacral wound and antibiotic teaching. Discharge likely Tuesday if afebrile on an oral antibiotic. He wants to return to work Wednesday from home.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Progress Note - Afternoon
notes.author: M. Kincaid, MD
notes.summary: Afebrile; no acetaminophen since 0430. Urine culture preliminary: gram-negative rods over 100,000 (1400). Continue ceftriaxone. Orthostatic drop at PT without the binder. CBC/CRP from 1700 pending.
notes.body:
**Subjective** Feels better. No headache since the morning. Lightheaded at therapy when sat up without the binder; fine with it.

**Objective** Afebrile since the morning; no acetaminophen since 0430. BP back in his baseline range. PT 1345: 98/60 lying, 76/46 after 3 minutes sitting without the binder and stockings (orthostatic); 90/56 with the binder snug, stockings on and a slow raise. Urine clearer.

**Results** Urine culture (1400, preliminary): greater than 100,000 CFU/mL gram-negative rods, identification to follow. Vitamin D 22 (insufficient). Prealbumin 14 (low, but CRP 112 this morning: inflammation lowers it). CBC and CRP drawn 1700, pending.

**Assessment and plan**
1. Complicated UTI: improving on ceftriaxone; next dose 2300; follow identification and susceptibilities.
2. Autonomic dysreflexia this morning: resolved; corrected call parameters in place.
3. Orthostatic hypotension: binder and stockings on before sitting; raise slowly.
4. Stage 2 sacrum: per the wound nurse; own cushion now here.
5. Indwelling catheter: physiatry recommends removal tonight and intermittent catheterization every 4 h; the removal criteria are in the catheter order.
6. AM labs ordered for 0500.

notes.author: N. Haverty, MD
notes.summary: Urine culture: E. coli over 100,000 (2200), susceptibilities pending. Blood cultures no growth at 24 hours. WBC 11.0, CRP 86 (improving). Continue ceftriaxone.
notes.body:
**Update** Urine culture at 2200: Escherichia coli, greater than 100,000 CFU/mL; susceptibilities to follow. Blood cultures: no growth at 24 hours.

**1700 labs** WBC 11.0 (from 13.1), CRP 86 (from 112): improving.

**Plan** Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV (due 2300). Change to an oral antibiotic by the susceptibilities. His home antibiotic (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) must not be assumed to work.

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Note - Antibiotic Change
notes.author: N. Haverty, MD
notes.summary: E. coli RESISTANT to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and ampicillin; susceptible to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Stop ceftriaxone; ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO every 12 h from 0900 to finish 7 days total. His usual home antibiotic would not have worked.
notes.body:
**Final susceptibilities (0230)** Escherichia coli: ampicillin R; ampicillin-sulbactam I; cefazolin S (urine breakpoint); ceftriaxone S; ciprofloxacin S; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole **R**; nitrofurantoin S; gentamicin S.

**Assessment** Febrile complicated E. coli UTI, improving: afebrile since Monday morning, WBC down to 11.0. Nitrofurantoin does not reach kidney tissue, so it is not used for a febrile (likely upper tract) infection. Ciprofloxacin is susceptible and is well absorbed by mouth.

**Plan**
- Stop ceftriaxone (last dose Mon 2300).
- Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO every 12 hours, first dose 0900, to complete 7 days total (through Sun 03/14 0900).
- Give 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium, magnesium, iron or zinc products (multivitamin with minerals).
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance noted for future UTIs; share with his SCI clinic.
- AM labs pending (0500 draw). Likely home today if he tolerates oral antibiotics and stays afebrile.
